thread:
alex: Heads-up — got an email that looked like a Redwood KMS console prompt asking me to re-auth. Link showed as https://login.redwood-kms[dot]com in the email. I clicked the link but did NOT enter creds. forwarding the full headers + screenshot.
kelly: Good catch, thanks for reporting. Don’t enter anything. Can you paste the original email headers and the raw URL here (or DM if you prefer)? We’ll submit the URL to the sandbox.
alex: Pasted headers and the URL: https://login.redwood-kms.com/auth?token=abc123 (clicked at 10:12 PDT). Screenshot uploaded. FYI the page looked very similar to our console — logo + signin form.
kelly: @rachel @tom FYI — potential credential harvesting site mimicking our KMS console. Alex says he clicked but didn’t provide creds.
safe-sandbox-bot: URL submitted to sandbox -> scan id sbox-2026-05-12-778. Initial results: redirect chain to login.redwood-kms.com -> cdn-assets[dot]verify-auth[dot]online -> mailer-tracking[dot]info. Behavior: credential-harvest-form detected. No binary malware. Full report: https://sandbox.internal/reports/sbox-2026-05-12-778 (access restricted).
rachel: Checking audit logs for any unusual KMS console API calls or IAM activity tied to alex. Running: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=Username,AttributeValue=alex@redwood.ai --region us-west-2` — will report back in 10m.
tom: Containment steps we should take ASAP: 1) Force SSO session revoke for alex (Okta/Azure AD) 2) Rotate any personal access keys tied to alex 3) Check for suspicious role assumption in the past 24h and revoke tokens if found. If alex used any service principal creds locally, rotate those.
kelly: Alex — can you confirm whether you had any CLI creds loaded when you clicked? `aws configure list` or `echo $AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` would tell us. If yes, log out/clear immediately.
alex: I had my laptop open with a long-lived CLI profile (dev-personal). I didn’t run any commands after clicking. `echo $AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` returned my access key id.
emily: Marking as higher risk then. We'll rotate alex's long-lived keys and force a logout. I’ll start key rotation for the user principal and any active tokens for the past 12h.
josh: Also: coordinate with infra to rotate any customer-managed KMS CMKs that might have been referenced by dev scripts? If keys were used only via roles then rotating user keys should be fine.
kelly: Action list updated: - revoke SSO sessions (tom) - rotate alex user keys (emily) - run CloudTrail + KMS access check (rachel) - submit domain to org blocklist and email gateway (security ops) - organization passwordless/2FA check and notify comms (josh)
safe-sandbox-bot: Sandbox final verdict: credential-harvest page + form posts to https://mailer-tracking.info/collect -> captured form fields: username, password, MFA_token (optional). Phishing kit fingerprints match campaign seen last month. Recommended: block domains, add sender hash to spam filter, escalate if any creds used.
rachel: CloudTrail scan: no KMS Decrypt/Encrypt calls from alex in the 24h window. There were 2 AWS STS:AssumeRole events from alex@redwood.ai 36h ago (expected for scheduled job), nothing suspicious now. No API calls to kms:GenerateDataKey or kms:Decrypt linked to alex since 10:00 PDT.
tom: Okta session revoke done for alex (revoked at 10:45 PDT). Confirmed his session invalidated.
emily: Rotated alex user access key pair, disabled old keys, created new ones and rotated locally. Logged rotation in internal ticket TICKET-9345. Also searched for that exact token string in internal logs — not found.
josh: Drafting a short company-wide note to go out in 1 hour: "Security alert: targeted credential-phishing campaign impersonating Redwood KMS console. No confirmed compromise. Do NOT enter credentials into any unexpected login pages. If you clicked and entered creds, immediately contact security." Will add recommended steps.
ankelly: (added) Let's also push a quick banner in the Console UI reminding users never to re-enter credentials outside of SSO flow. Can engineering ops put up a temporary banner?
emily: I can add a temporary banner referencing the SSO flow + link to security policy. Will coordinate with product for wording.
kelly: Severity: LOW-MED given no confirmed exfil and no API activity. Containment: complete (SSO revoke, user key rotation, domain block). Post-incident: internal note + phishing awareness email + blocklist update + add domain to spam filter. Close after awareness mail sent and banner up.
josh: Nice work team. Add follow-up: run a search for any other clicks to login.redwood-kms.com in the email gateway in past 7 days and report count.
alex: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick response. I did not put any creds in so hopefully minimal impact.
kelly: Closing thread once comms sent. Will attach sandbox report & ticket id. :white_check_mark:
